We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our research groups at the KAIST School of Computing in Daejeon, South Korea. The fellow will be co-advised by Joseph Seering and Juho Kim. The focus of the postdoc position will be multi-agent systems with applications in modeling and simulating social behaviors.

The fellow is expected to drive a research agenda in this area. Example responsibilities and topics include, but are not limited to:

• Developing and leading research projects in multi-agent systems and social simulation.
• Actively participating in research group activities and lab culture.
• Assisting in writing research proposals.

This position is strictly research-focused; the postdoc will not have a teaching role.

Duration & Start Date: The duration of the postdoc is one year, starting in late summer or early Fall 2026. Extension beyond one year may be possible contingent on available postdoc funding and alignment of research goals. Expected compensation is approximately 80,000,000 KRW for one year (to be paid monthly) plus benefits standard for the position.

Required Qualifications:

• PhD successfully defended.
• PhD in Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Information Science, or a related field.
• Experience conducting and publishing research in top-tier HCI and/or NLP venues (such as CHI, CSCW, *ACL, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience collaborating directly with social scientists.

The chosen candidate must pass the official KAIST screening processes and, if applicable, clear all visa requirements before beginning employment.

Application:
Please submit the following to

. Materials received by June 15th AoE will be given priority, but review will continue until the position is filled.

• Research statement that outlines research achievements and future research agenda, including (brief) preliminary plans for postdoctoral research
• Two representative publications that show alignment with this position’s focus
• CV
• Names and contact information of three references. References may be contacted for shortlisted candidates, but recommendation letters are not required at initial application.
